messages:
ana: deploy-bot just fired a canary p95 alert for v3.6.0 (p95 ~ 610ms). We have two Dedicated pools in the path. Recommend holding auto-revert.

deploy-bot: Alert: p95 > 500ms for 3m on canary slice. Policy recommends autorevert to 3.5.2.

chris: If autorevert happens it will affect Dedicated customers. Can we suppress auto and do a surgical canary rollback + pin?

ops-bot: @ana hold applied: suppressing auto-rollback for 12 minutes. Manual action recommended.

marco: Quick log snippet: 
```
[2026-06-02T08:22:10Z] runtime: kvcache miss -> quantization fallback -> latency 720ms
[2026-06-02T08:22:11Z] frontend: upstream 10.4.2.7:502 
```

ana: Plan: 1) rollback canary slice to 3.5.2, 2) pin Dedicated pools to 3.5.2, 3) send CS note, 4) open post-mortem. Chris, can you run?

chris: Running commands now:
```
redwoodctl rollout rollback --service=inference --to-version=3.5.2 --slice=canary --reason="post-canary tail latency"
redwoodctl routes pin --route=dedicated-global --version=3.5.2 --note="protect-customer-routes"
```

ops-bot: ACTION: rollback initiated by chris at 2026-06-02T08:24:02Z. job id rb-4743210000-1

chris: Canary rollback completed. Quick smoke: p95 -> 125ms, 502s cleared.

cs: Sending customer brief: "During a canary rollout we detected increased tail latency affecting a small subset of traffic. We rolled the canary back and pinned Dedicated routes to the prior stable release. No action required; full post-mortem to follow."

ana: OK. Next steps: eng to triage kernel/quant path, revert risky kernel selector for next candidate. Update release notes: mark v3.6.0 as paused and reference rollback. I'll open the post-mortem ticket and attach logs + commands.

deploy-bot: Manual rollback recorded. Recommend CI run that validates kernel selector before next rollout.

ana: Closing thread. If any regression, ping here or @ops. :white_check_mark:
